prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right one depends on your goals, budget, industry, and whether you need enterprise-level strategy, performance marketing, creative/brand work, or technical execution (SEO, paid media, analytics, UX, etc.).

To help you pick, I can:
- Shortlist agencies that match your needs
- Provide interview questions, an RFP template, and evaluation criteria
- Help compare proposals

Quick questions so I can make a tailored shortlist:
1. What are your top goals? (e.g., increase MQLs, lower CAC, grow organic traffic, launch product)
2. What channels matter most? (SEO, paid search, paid social, content, email, CRO, creative/brand, web dev)
3. What’s your monthly/annual marketing budget or retainer range?
4. Company stage and type: startup, SMB, enterprise, B2B or B2C, industry vertical?
5. Do you need an agency with technical capabilities (e.g., analytics/Tag Manager, GTM, data engineering) or more creative/brand work?

If you want a quick, general starting list of reputable agencies that are active in the Bay Area (you can evaluate these based on the questions above):
- R/GA — strong on brand, creative and product experience design for large clients
- AKQA — creative, digital product and brand work at enterprise level
- Razorfish — digital transformation, integrated digital strategy and marketing
- Huge — UX/experience design plus digital strategy for larger brands
- Jellyfish — performance marketing and training, global agency model
- Wpromote — performance marketing focused on mid-market to enterprise paid/social
- Seer Interactive — SEO and analytics-driven marketing (data-focused)
- Metric Theory / other performance-specialists — paid search and performance media

How to evaluate agencies (quick checklist):
- Relevant case studies and measurable results for businesses like yours
- Transparent pricing and clear deliverables/KPIs
- Team composition and dedicated resources (PM, strategist, creatives, analysts)
- Reporting cadence and data/attribution approach
- Contract flexibility and trial period / pilot project option
- Client references you can call

Sample interview questions to ask any agency:
- What specific results have you generated for companies like ours? Can you share metrics?
- Which channels would you prioritize and why?
- Who will be our day-to-day contact and who will do the actual work?
- What tools/platforms do you use for tracking, reporting, and bidding?
- How do you approach attribution and measuring ROI?
- What is your onboarding process and typical timeline for seeing results?

If you want, tell me the answers to those five questions above and I’ll recommend a short list of 3–5 agencies in San Francisco that best fit your needs — plus draft an email/RFP you can send them.
